A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same RHO research work and complete, readable main text and supplementary Sections A–E. Both have 14 pages; pages 3–14 match in extracted text and rendered appearance.

before.justification: v1 reports original localization experiments on CV-RHO, cross-region and Sim2Real evaluations, and component ablations in Tables 3–8.

after.justification: v2 retains the original localization experiments, cross-region and Sim2Real evaluations, and ablation results in Tables 3–8.

M1.justification: The two-branch Pin–Pan architecture, Split-Undistort-Merge module, and Position-Orientation Fusion procedure remain identical in Section 3.3 and supplementary Section D.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same CV-RHO cities and clean/adverse conditions, Mount Vernon cross-region evaluation, and Sim2Real testing in Ogori, Detroit, and Hasselt.

E2.justification: OrienterNet remains the external comparator in Tables 3–6, with identical field-of-view variants in Table 3. The fusion comparison methods in Table 8 are also unchanged.

E3.justification: The reported 8:2 data split, 10k-image cross-region and 5k-image Sim2Real test sets, recall thresholds, training settings, and evaluation procedures are unchanged, including supplementary details.

E4.justification: Both retain the same adverse-condition, cross-region, and Sim2Real analyses, plus the BEV merge and fusion ablations in Section 4.3 and Tables 7–8. No analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both report results without repeated-run uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The image-generation seed of 42 disclosed in supplementary Section B is unchanged.

E6.justification: All result entries in Tables 3–8 and the plotted findings in Figure 1 are unchanged. For example, Table 3 reports RHO PR@5m of 84.36% and OR@5° of 90.44% in both versions.

T1.justification: The pose definition, gravity and coordinate assumptions, Shannon entropy formula, and fusion equations remain identical in Sections 3.1 and 3.3. No mathematical derivation or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: Both retain the same claims concerning the first large-scale robust OSM-based MCVGL benchmark, the RHO architecture and modules, and performance gains up to 20%. Introduction edits do not alter their scope.

C2.justification: The explanations of panoramic positioning and pinhole orientation, generalization and Sim2Real interpretations, and supplementary limitations remain unchanged, including restricted pinhole-only applicability and limited exploitation of training diversity.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 and supplementary Sections A–D retain identical hardware, optimization settings, batch sizes, generation prompts and parameters, and collection details. The project access link is unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion and all 74 references are unchanged. The paper retains the same positioning relative to OSM-based, robust, and panoramic localization research.

P1.justification: v2 expands the INSAIT affiliation to include Sofia University, lightly shortens the introductory dataset and performance descriptions, uses the MCVGL abbreviation, and changes 'original image' to 'original images'. Section organization is unchanged.

P2.justification: The affiliation block expands to two lines, shifting the abstract and Figure 1 downward and reflowing introductory text across pages 1–2. Figure and table content is unchanged; pages 3–14 render identically.

improvement.justification: v2 supplies a fuller affiliation and small wording edits, accompanied by limited text reflow. The methods, evidence, claims, reproducibility information, and appendices are unchanged. These editorial differences do not materially improve or diminish the paper's overall quality.
